content: SIMCOR tablets are a combination medication that contains niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) and simvastatin. Simvastatin is an inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, and both simvastatin and niacin are agents that modify lipid levels. Niacin, also known as nicotinic acid or 3-pyridinecarboxylic acid, is a white, non-hygroscopic crystalline powder. It is highly soluble in water, boiling ethanol, and propylene glycol, but it is insoluble in ethyl ether. The structural formula of niacin is provided in the original documentation. Simvastatin is chemically described as butanoic acid, 2,2-dimethyl-, 1,2,3,7,8,8a-hexahydro-3,7-dimethyl-8-[1-naphthalenyl] ester. It appears as a white to off-white, non-hygroscopic crystalline powder. Simvastatin is practically insoluble in water but freely soluble in chloroform, methanol, and ethanol. Its structural formula is also provided in the original documentation. SIMCOR is available as oral tablets in the following strengths: 500 mg of niacin extended-release (NIASPAN) and 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 500/20 mg), 500 mg of niacin extended-release and 40 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 500/40 mg), 750 mg of niacin extended-release and 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 750/20 mg), 1000 mg of niacin extended-release and 20 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 1000/20 mg), 1000 mg of niacin extended-release and 40 mg of simvastatin (SIMCOR 1000/40 mg). Each tablet also contains the following inactive ingredients: hypromellose, povidone, stearic acid, polyethylene glycol, butylated hydroxyanisole, FD&C Blue 2, lactose monohydrate, titanium dioxide, and triacetin. Additionally, SIMCOR 500/20 mg, SIMCOR 750/20 mg, and SIMCOR 1000/20 mg formulations include iron oxide.
